overview.tell: The sky is the same warm ochre as the dirt road — zenith (185,162,147), hue 27 deg, blue the LOWEST channel at every altitude, and only 6 LSB of zenith-to-horizon luma change (185 -> 191) — which together with 75.5% of all pixels sitting inside a single 55-degree warm hue wedge and 0.1% of the frame anywhere in green (80-160 deg) makes this read as a sepia photographic filter laid over a 3D render, not Valkyria's sage/cream/teal palette.

fixes.system: src/world/sky.js (SKY.zenith / SKY.horizon at :208-212, cloud shading at :159-160)
fixes.problem: Round 1 fix #4 asked for a muted teal-grey zenith (~0x7f9ba3), >=45 luma delta zenith-to-horizon and >=12% chroma at zenith. The opposite shipped. Measured across x=100-800: y=10 (185.3,161.7,146.7) sat 0.21 B-R -38.6; y=110 (183.8,160.2,143.6); y=210 (197.8,172.9,136.2) sat 0.31 B-R -61.6; y=310 (190.6,167.6,137.7). Zenith-to-horizon delta is 6 LSB, hue is 27 deg (warm brown), and blue is the lowest channel everywhere — zero teal in the entire dome. Clouds now exist (sky patch stdev 15.52, up from round 1's 4.49) but they are soft-alpha airbrushed horizontal smears: the round-1 request to quantise them was not applied, the two smoothsteps at :159-160 (smoothstep(0.10,0.50,litQ) then smoothstep(0.46,0.86,litQ)) are continuous ramps. This single surface is 28% of the frame and it is what collapses the whole palette into sepia: at sat>0.3 (51% of all pixels) 98% of hues fall in 15-60 deg.
fixes.change: Set SKY.zenith = 0x7d97a4 and SKY.horizon = 0xe8d8b4. Replace the cloud lit ramp with a 3-step quantiser driven by the same bleed noise the world uses: `float lq = floor(litQ * 3.0 + vcFbm3(sUv * 3.1) * 0.22) / 3.0; vec3 cloud = mix(uCloudShade, uCloudMid, smoothstep(0.28,0.38,lq)); cloud = mix(cloud, uCloudLit, smoothstep(0.61,0.71,lq));`. Verification: mean of a[10,100:800] must satisfy B > R, and mean luma at y=10 must differ from y=310 by >= 40 LSB.

fixes.system: src/render/canvasRenderPipeline.js:765-772 (paper composite) + src/render/textures.js:161-185 (getPaperTexture)
fixes.problem: The substrate is a machine-regular ruled screen and it is loudest exactly where the rubric says it must vanish. `mid = pow(1.0 - abs(l*2.0-1.0), 0.75)` evaluates to 0.52 on the lit cream stucco (l = 0.79), so the fibre multiply runs at half strength on the brightest surface in frame. Measured on clean stucco (y215-290, x640-760, meanLuma 201): high-pass sd 8.83 — the same amplitude as the midtone grass (7.29) — with an orientation-power anisotropy of 36.5:1 at an 8.6 px period. The lit retaining wall (y470-600, x1420-1700, luma 159) measures 62.8:1 — a near-perfect single-direction halftone. The dark grass band (luma 109), where graphite SHOULD dominate, measures only 7.4:1. The cause is getPaperTexture's `fibre` term: two crossing 4:1-anisotropic fbms weighted 0.30 into the R output at :182, which produces ruled lines rather than cold-press tooth.
fixes.change: Replace the mid term with `float mid = smoothstep(0.96, 0.60, l) * smoothstep(0.06, 0.24, l);` and multiply by `(1.0 - 0.75 * isSkyC)` using the sky mask already reconstructed at :632. In getPaperTexture, drop the fibre stretch from 4:1 to 1.6:1 and rebalance :182 to `lum = sat(0.60 + (tooth-0.5)*0.58 + (fibre-0.5)*0.12 + (grain-0.5)*0.16)`. Verification: high-pass sd on the stucco patch must fall below 3.0 and its orientation anisotropy below 4.0:1, while the grass shadow band (y700-830, x850-1050) stays above 10.

fixes.system: src/actors/character.js:1044 + actorBodyMaterial / actorGearMaterial (src/actors/rig.js), against src/world/worldMaterials.js:186-188
fixes.problem: Round 1 fix #3's verification was 'the shadow-side sample must satisfy B > R'. The world got it — terrain shadow is now (85,83,96), hue 249 deg, B-R +11, versus round 1's warm (85,80,64) — because worldMaterials.js:186-188 now runs `npShadeCol = mix(npBase*uShadeTint, uShadeTint, 0.55)` with `npShadeCol.b = max(npShadeCol.b, npShadeCol.r*1.10)`. Characters never enter that path and are unfixed. Hero tunic lit (187,152,104) hue 34 deg vs shade (128,101,86) hue 21 deg, B-R -42 — the shade is WARMER than the light. The near-left soldier is worse: lit back (207,166,124) hue 31 val 81%, shade side (191,154,118) hue 29 val 75% — a 6% value drop and a 2-degree hue drop across the entire form, i.e. the largest figure in frame has no terminator at all and is lit by a flat wash.
fixes.change: Route actorBodyMaterial() and actorGearMaterial() through the same nprUniforms/NPR_BODY factory the world uses, passing shadeTint 0x4b4270, bands 3, bandBleed 0.13, and raise the key gain so the half-Lambert drive across a 0.35 m torso spans at least two band boundaries. Verification: sample a 7x7 mean at (x=105, y=760) — it must return B > R and a hue above 200 deg — and a horizontal scan across the near soldier's back at y=700 must show >= 2 steps of > 12 LSB (it currently shows a 176->158->204 wander whose largest interior step on the tunic is 6).

fixes.system: src/world/vegetation.js:940-960 (trunk instanced meshes) + src/render/materials.js band drive
fixes.problem: Round 1 fix #5 demanded tapered trunks with bark, root flare and a contact shadow. The trunk geometry is a swept tapered tube in _buildTree, but on screen it renders as a flat unshaded bar and none of the material work landed. The nearest and largest vertical object in frame (x 1330-1385) has a horizontal cross-section at y=660 of 108,109,108,108,109,109,109,109,109,109,110,110,111,111,111,113,113,113 — a ~40 px wide, roughly 0.5 m diameter cylinder in direct sunlight rendered as ONE value varying 5 LSB across its full diameter, and the column at x=1355 holds 104-110 for 310 px of height. Zero terminator, zero band boundary, no bark, no root flare, and it meets the terrain with no contact darkening. The only modulation on it is the 12 px ruled paper screen (anisotropy 14:1), which is why it reads as a flat purple bar.
fixes.change: Add the trunk bin to the nprUniforms path with bands: 3, bandBleed: 0.13 and a detailMap: a triplanar bark map at 0.12 m vertical / 0.045 m circumferential tiling multiplied at 0.22 strength with per-instance UV rotation. Add a root-flare skirt (radius * 1.55 at the base, decaying over 0.4 m) and a radial contact-shadow decal of radius 1.3 * trunkR at the terrain junction. Verification: a horizontal scan across the trunk at y=660 must show >= 2 steps of > 12 LSB and an interior lumaSD above 14.

fixes.system: src/world/vegetation.js (near reed/grass LOD outline flag) + src/render/canvasRenderPipeline.js thin-geometry resolve
fixes.problem: Round 1 fix #5 asked for userData.outlineWidth 0.4 on the near grass LOD. Not applied. In the crop (x820-1060, y600-760) every foreground reed is a hard-aliased flat triangle with visible stair-step jaggies on both edges and no ink whatsoever, and every thin stalk and overhead wire renders as a broken 1-px dotted line of alternating pale and background pixels. Measured: 10,983 pixels (0.530% of the frame) deviate more than 25 LSB from their own 3x3 median, and 2,995 deviate more than 40; the far-field band (y330-470, x60-560) hits 0.727%. These are isolated single-pixel outliers, i.e. sub-pixel geometry sparkle that will crawl violently under any camera motion — an automatic rejection under both 'aliased edges' and 'lines must not crawl or shimmer'.
fixes.change: Set userData.outlineWidth = 0.4 and route the near reed material through nprUniforms with bands: 3 so blades take ink and quantised shading. Independently, clamp thin geometry to a minimum screen width in the vertex stage — expand the blade/wire quad along its screen-space normal so its projected width never falls below 2.0 CSS px (`float w = max(worldW, 2.0 * gl_Position.w * uPxToWorld);`) — and render the thin bin with alpha-to-coverage against a 4x MSAA target before the outline composite. Verification: fraction of pixels with |L - median3| > 25 must drop below 0.10% frame-wide and below 0.15% in the far-field patch.

fixes.system: src/actors/character.js buildBody / buildGear (pouch, boot, arm) and src/actors/rig.js skin weights
fixes.problem: The forms are much improved over round 1's tan mannequin — there are now boots, hands, a rifle and webbing — but four primitive tells remain on the two largest figures. (a) Both soldiers carry a hip pouch that is a flat, axis-aligned, straight-edged rectangle: the hero's measures (157,141,155) over a tight interior with lumaSD 7.51 and a total range of 28 LSB across the whole quad — an untextured primitive with a uniform fill and a uniform outline, the most obviously '3D box' object in frame. (b) The near soldier's feet are two flat brown slabs lying on the ground plane with no heel, no toe box and no last, reading as slippers; the left one is not planted. (c) His right arm is a single lozenge from shoulder to hand with no elbow bend anywhere in its silhouette. (d) The torso-to-hip transition pinches abruptly — a candy-wrapper joint, which the rubric names explicitly.
fixes.change: Replace the pouch quad with a bevelled box (0.02 m chamfer) carrying a canvas-weave detail map at 0.006 m tiling plus a modelled flap and buckle, and give it bands: 3 through nprUniforms. Model the boot as a proper last: heel block 0.03 m, toe box swept over 3 rings, sole plate inset 0.012 m, and snap the ankle IK target to terrain.heightAt() with a foot-roll solve so both feet are planted. Insert an elbow joint at 0.52 of the humerus-to-wrist span with a 12-degree default flexion so the arm silhouette bends. Spread the torso-to-hip skin weights over 2 extra vertex rings. Verification: the pouch region must show >= 2 quantised bands and an outline width varying at least 1.8:1 between its silhouette and its interior creases.

closeup.tell: The whole frame is a two-hue sepia duotone — sky (222,198,163) h35.6, cloud h36.0, lit canopy h37.1, lit grass h34.8 and the road h36.0 all land within 2.3 degrees of hue 36, only 17,831 of 2,073,600 pixels (0.86%) are green-dominant, and just 0.25% of sampled pixels fall anywhere in hue 70-200 at sat>0.10, so Gallia's sage/olive countryside and teal-grey sky have been laundered into one amber wash with a mauve shadow wash and nothing else.

fixes.system: src/render/materials.js:959 (lightBias for skinning) + :516 drive remap + :951 bands
fixes.problem: ROUND 1's HEADLINE DEFECT IS STILL PRESENT, with the opposite sign. The face no longer ramps — it is now ONE FLAT WASH with no terminator at all. Skin-only histogram of x975-1085,y425-500 is unimodal, peaking 149-154 with 4,600 of 6,348 samples inside 145-159; the cheek row y=460, x970-1080 runs 145.9-156.9 over 110 px and every step above 3 LSB is a drawn hair/whisker stroke, not a lighting boundary. Cause is the round-1 fix over-correcting: `drive = clamp((drive-0.46)*1.26 + 0.46 + 0.13)` with bands:3 means the raw drive must fall below 0.521 to cross the upper boundary, and a wrap-0.40 half-Lambert on a skull under a near-frontal key never gets there — so instead of the head sliding into the darkest band it now sits entirely inside the LIGHTEST one. Zero band boundaries anywhere on the head, jaw, nose or neck.
fixes.change: Set lightBias for skinning from 0.13 to 0.0 and contrast from 1.26 to 1.85, and before the remap normalise the key per material: `drive = (drive - uDriveMin) / max(uDriveMax - uDriveMin, 0.05)` with uDriveMin/uDriveMax pushed from the material factory as the object's expected key span (0.28/0.86 for skin). Add a curvature term so a smooth skull crosses a boundary on form rather than only on N.L: `drive -= 0.16 * clamp(length(fwidth(N))*uCurvGain, 0.0, 1.0)`. Verification: a horizontal scanline across the cheek at y=460 must contain at least one step of >=25 LSB whose two sides are each flat within +/-3 LSB over >=15 px, and the skin histogram must be bimodal with the two modes >=30 LSB apart.

fixes.system: src/render/canvasRenderPipeline.js:744-761 (split tone + saturation shaping), :972 uHighTint, :966 uPaperWhite
fixes.problem: The grade collapses every albedo onto one hue. `c *= mix(vec3(1.0), hT, smoothstep(0.48, 1.0, l))` with uHighTint 0xfff0d2 applies the cream tint to essentially the whole frame, because the frame's median luma is 0.55+ — sky 178, lit grass 190, road 236. The saturation block then multiplies foliage green by 0.89 and ochre by 1.10 on top, so what little green survives the tint is actively suppressed while the amber is boosted. Result: river measures (167-200,164-195,142-172) = hue 47-60, sat 0.13 — a khaki sandbar, not water; the greenest pixel in the entire image is (181,186,109). Separately 16,483 pixels clip R=255 (sky reaches (255,219,164)), which flattens the highlight and forces the hue further toward amber.
fixes.change: Move the highlight tint out of the general midtones: `smoothstep(0.48, 1.0, l)` -> `smoothstep(0.80, 1.0, l)` and desaturate uHighTint 0xfff0d2 -> 0xfaf3e6. Delete the ochre boost entirely (`hsv.y *= 1.0 + ochreness * 0.10` and `hsv.z *= 1.0 + ochreness * 0.030`) and invert the green term to a protection: `hsv.y *= 1.0 + greenness * 0.18`, widening the green lobe to exp(-dg*dg/0.020) so sage at hue 85-115 is preserved rather than shaved. Lower uExposure 1.06 -> 0.96 and uPaperWhite 0xfff6e4 -> 0xf6ecd8 so no channel clips. Verification: >=8% of frame pixels must have hue in 70-160 at sat>0.12, the sky patch must measure B>=R-10 (teal-grey), and R==255 count must be 0.

fixes.system: src/actors/character.js (head/face feature build, hand + forearm rig) and src/actors/rig.js
fixes.problem: The hero's head does not read as a head at 2 m. The hair is a dark irregular paint-splat plastered across the MIDDLE of the near cheek (sampled (83,59,75) at 960,470) with a second detached blob on the jaw; there is no ear, only a pale blue-grey chip; the mouth is a bean-shaped blob sitting ON the profile silhouette at (1080,485) rather than inside the face; the jaw is a lumpy potato with no mandible line; and the eye carries a saturated amber rim — (175,123,96) to (195,143,109), sat 0.43-0.45 at x1101-1105,y432-436, the highest-chroma pixels on the entire character — which reads as lens flare, not an eyelid. The right forearm is a smooth featureless tube ending in a mitten with no separated fingers; the left hand at (868-959, 1007-1080) is a set of parallel sausage strips that the rifle fore-end passes straight through. The 12 m second soldier has no face at all (head patch 1300,585,36x40 measures mean 101.5 sd 41.2 with the whole face side in one dark blob).
fixes.change: Move the hairline into a mesh-space mask keyed to a scalp UV so hair cannot project onto the cheek plane — clamp its lower bound to v >= 0.62 of head height on the near side and to the ear line on the far side. Model the ear as geometry with an inked helix rather than a shading patch. Anchor the mouth to a face-local landmark (0.18 head-height above the chin, inset 0.04 from the profile) instead of screen-projecting it onto the silhouette. Drop the amber eye rim entirely — draw the upper lash as an ink stroke in the outline weight channel at 1.5 CSS px minimum, colour uInkFloor, not a saturated albedo ring. For the hands, solve two-bone IK to the weapon grip and fore-end sockets and close the proximal phalanges to the stock radius so the fingers wrap; add a depth-test pass so no finger renders in front of the barrel it is supposed to be behind.

fixes.system: src/render/materials.js (hatch block) + src/render/shaderLib.js GLSL_HATCH, CFG.render.hatchStrength 0.62
fixes.problem: The hatch is a single-direction machine ruling. In the shadow band it runs at one fixed angle (~-35 deg) at constant spacing across the terrain, the grass blades, the rifle stock and the hero's tunic at identical amplitude — no crossing direction anywhere in the frame, no per-stroke pressure variation, no start/stop jitter. Autocorrelation of a shadow row at y=940, x1400-1750 decays monotonically (lags 2-20: 366, 324, 287, 254, 229, 206, 189, 175, 160, 133, 104, 82, 78, 77, 76, 76, 72, 65, 56) with no secondary peak, i.e. it is a uniform screen rather than a drawn field. It reads as a printed halftone laid over the shadow, which is the round-1 'firefight' note re-appearing unfixed.
fixes.change: Inside vcHatchField perturb per stroke: `angle += 0.16 * (vcFbm2(sPx * 0.0035) - 0.5)` and `spacing *= 1.0 + 0.30 * (vcFbm2(sPx * 0.0021 + 91.0) - 0.5)`, and modulate opacity along the stroke by `vcFbm2(sPx * 0.02)` so pressure varies. Add a genuine second direction at +72 deg, seeded from an independent hash (not an offset of the first field so the two cannot phase-lock), weighted 1.0 in the darkest band and 0.0 in the second. Gate the whole thing off surfaces closer than 0.9 m of screen-space stroke width so a 12 px rifle stock does not get the same ruling as a 400 px hillside.

fixes.system: src/world/structures.js + src/world/worldMaterials.js (stuccoGrey / tileA / tileB / plaster) and src/world/textures.js
fixes.problem: Untextured primitives, unchanged since round 1. The half-timbered house at 45 m is one flat lavender-grey stucco fill ((155,129,123), patch 660,300,200x160 sd 25.6 almost all of it from the window rectangles), the roof is a flat brick-red gradient with zero tile courses, the timber frame is flat strips and the windows are flat rectangles with no glazing bars, reveal or damage. It also carries NO ink at all: the wall corner at y=380 steps 184.3 -> 133.1 in a single pixel with no dark trough, while a tree canopy 20 m nearer gets a 3 px stroke at 87 LSB depth (row y=200: 197.1 -> 122.7 -> 111.6 -> 110.4 -> 129.5). The stone wall in the midground is a flat field with scattered light rectangles, and the road is one uninterrupted cream plane spanning the middle third.
fixes.change: Add a triplanar detail map to the masonry/stucco material at 0.55 m world tile multiplied at 0.20 strength, and a tile-course map on roofs with rows every 0.14 m plus per-row ochre/umber jitter of +/-8%, authored in src/world/textures.js alongside bladeTexture. Add per-face albedo jitter of +/-6% hashed from the face centroid. Give the house bin userData.outlineWidth 0.8 with the same depth-graded ink falloff the character uses so 45 m architecture keeps a hairline rather than none. Scatter cart ruts, a puddle decal and 8-12 gravel/timber props along the road spline in src/world/layout.js. Verification: no 300x160 patch in the midground with meanEdge below 6.

fixes.system: src/render/canvasRenderPipeline.js outline depth ramp + haze uniforms, and CFG.render.chroma 0.0016 / VC_CA at :713
fixes.problem: Two atmosphere failures. (a) Aerial perspective runs backwards: the 30 m stone wall is the sharpest, most contrasty thing in frame at meanEdge 15.43 / high-pass sd 8.08, against the 2 m hero face at 12.01 / 5.38 and the hero's tunic at 6.50 / 3.54 — the focal subject of a CLOSEUP carries less drawn incident than a wall 30 m behind it, and the 12 m second soldier's head measures 23.68, twice the hero's face. (b) Chromatic aberration is still on. The telegraph wires produce isolated saturated pixels — (114,46,67) hue 342 sat 0.60 at (1632,60) and (196,89,59) hue 13 sat 0.70 at (1898,28) — the two highest-saturation pixels in the whole image, against a cream sky of (253,215,160). The wire itself is a broken stipple ((114,66,78), (204,163,143), (187,134,110), (242,201,166) at 4 px spacing) that will crawl in motion. Round 1 flagged the identical artefact at 176,38,41; chroma was reduced to 0.0016 but not eliminated, and the fringe peak is now MORE saturated than it was.
fixes.change: (a) Multiply ink opacity and lerp uInk toward uHazeColor by `smoothstep(0.04, 0.30, c.lz)` so 30 m linework goes grey-violet at ~0.25 density, and raise the haze so the mid-ground desaturates — target the 30 m wall patch below meanEdge 9 and high-pass sd below 5, i.e. under the hero. Independently raise near-field detail on the character so hero-tunic meanEdge exceeds 11. (b) Set CFG.render.chroma to 0.0 and drop `if (this.quality >= 1) gd.VC_CA = ''` at :1079 entirely. Replace the sub-pixel telegraph wires with a screen-space-widened line primitive clamped to a 1.4 CSS px minimum drawn in uInkFloor so the run is continuous instead of a stipple. Verification: max per-pixel saturation in the top-right 300x300 quadrant must fall below 0.40.

bridge.tell: Every submerged pier is a transparent X-ray box: the riverbed inside pier 1 measures meanRGB (165.2,160.6,140.8) against (165.9,157.6,136.8) for open bed 95 px to its left — a sub-4-LSB delta, i.e. the masonry volume contributes zero pigment — while its silhouette AND its hidden rear bottom edge are still stroked in full-weight graphite, so the piers read as inked wireframe cages standing in the water.

fixes.system: src/world/water.js:236-241 (transparent/depthWrite:false) + src/world/structures.js:497-527 (pier loft) + the outline composite in src/render/canvasRenderPipeline.js
fixes.problem: The river is transparent with depthWrite:false, and the comment at structures.js:500-513 admits the consequence — 'anything submerged still gets a full-weight graphite outline drawn over the water by the composite'. The team's response was to delete the submerged geometry's SHADE rather than its INK, so below the waterline the pier is now pure outline over bare riverbed: patch (950,800,70x80) inside pier 1 reads meanRGB (165.2,160.6,140.8) versus (165.9,157.6,136.8) for open bed at (855,800,70x80) — 0.7/3.0/4.0 LSB of difference — and the far bottom-back edge of the box is visible straight through the front face. A stray vertical ink line also hangs from the cutwater to the bed at x=1049. Separately there is still no reflection and no waterline contact: scanning y=800 across the pier gives 115, then the 3-px ink line 55,55,56, then 143,175,179 — the water jumps straight to the brightest value in the row with zero contact darkening, and water beside the pier (1060,760,120x60) meanL 146.9 vs open water (1560,760,120x60) meanL 159.3 is pure distance falloff carrying no bridge silhouette.
fixes.change: Give the river a depth pre-pass (render the plane to depth only with colorWrite:false before the transparent sheet, keeping depthWrite:false on the visible pass) and write its depth into the id/G-buffer. In the composite, multiply outline opacity by exp(-3.2 * max(0, waterDepth - fragDepth)) so ink dies within ~0.3 m of submergence instead of being full weight at 2 m. Then restore the pier shaft as an OPAQUE solid from waterRel-0.45 down to the bed in structures.js:505 (loft the same hexagonal plan to baseY, setGeomColor to PALETTE.stone mixed 0.55 toward PALETTE.mud) so it occludes the bed. Add the planar reflection the shot's own docstring promises: render bins.stone into a 512x256 mirror RT about the water plane, blend 0.30 with a 6 px vertical smear, and darken a 0.25 m band either side of every pier waterline by 0.78. Verification: interior patch (950,800,70x80) must differ from (855,800,70x80) by >25 LSB in at least one channel, and the y=800 scan must show a >20 LSB dip in the 8 px immediately downstream of the pier.

fixes.system: src/render/materials.js:490-492 (drive += blotch) feeding vcQuantiseBands at :534
fixes.problem: The quantiser exists and is never observable. drive += (wash-0.5)*uBlotch*0.090 + (gran-0.5)*uBlotch*0.038 injects a two-octave noise (the fine octave is at uBlotchScale*3.7, i.e. a few screen px) with a peak-to-peak amplitude comparable to a whole band of width 1/uBands = 0.25, so the boundary is shredded into per-pixel salt and no plateau survives to screen. Measured: a 31-px-box horizontal sweep across the full 310 px barrel vault at y=700 wanders 89.1 -> 126.9 with mean |dL/dx| 1.56 LSB/px, max step 7.6, and the longest run flat to +/-2 LSB is 14 samples; the 900x380 bridge-stone mass has a UNIMODAL luma histogram (single mode at L=123, 3.06%); a 21-px-box vertical scan of the near bank at x=950 gives mean |dL/dy| 2.86 with two plateaus in 135 samples. Round 1's headline defect — a smooth luminance ramp with zero plateaus — is still present, unchanged, on every surface I sampled.
fixes.change: Take the blotch out of the band drive entirely: delete both `drive +=` lines at :490-491 and apply (wash-0.5)*uBlotch*0.10 as a post-quantisation multiply on `col` AFTER the two-tone grade at :547-548, where it modulates pigment without moving a boundary. If a boundary wander is still wanted, feed only the LOW-frequency octave (blot.r at uBlotchScale, never the 3.7x fine term) into the existing wetBands displacement at :528 and cap it at min(dPerPx*uWetPx, 0.30). Verification: a 31-px-box scan across the barrel vault (x 700..1010 at y=700) must show >=3 runs of >=25 consecutive samples flat to +/-2 LSB, and the bridge-stone luma histogram over (350,420,900x380) must show >=3 modes separated by >=14 LSB.

fixes.system: src/render/materials.js:547-548 (`col = mix(shadeCol, midCol, smoothstep(0.02,0.46,g))`) + uViolet, and setSun(ctx, 0.17, -1.72) in src/game/captureShots.js:385
fixes.problem: PALETTE.stone is 0xa39a8c — a warm grey (163,154,140) — yet every stone pixel in the frame renders violet: lit spandrel (126,111,143) hue 268 sat 0.22, arch intrados (89,74,101) hue 273, retaining wall (141,125,157) hue 270. Lit and shade are the SAME hue at 0.68 value ratio, so there is no terminator and no warm/cool split anywhere on the object that occupies ~35% of the canvas. The cause is structural: the shot deliberately parks the visible east face in the shade band (captureShots.js:383-385), that face lands on band index 1, and smoothstep(0.02,0.46,0.25) = 0.42 leaves it 58% shadeCol — precisely the failure the comment at materials.js:541-546 says was already fixed. The ambient re-tint at :560 stacks a second cool pass on top.
fixes.change: Change the mid ramp to `smoothstep(0.02, 0.28, g)` so band index 1 resolves to 0.94 midCol (<=6% shade contamination) and only index 0 may be violet-dominated, and drop the ambient tint weight at :560 from 0.30 to 0.12. Re-aim the key in captureShots.bridge(): setSun(ctx, 0.17, -1.72) -> setSun(ctx, 0.21, -0.55) so the camera-facing spandrel takes a genuine lit band and the voussoir ring and parapet throw the shadows the docstring already claims. Verification: lit spandrel hue must fall in [35,55] with sat <=0.20, the shaded intrados must satisfy B > R*1.05 with hue in [255,285], and the two must differ by >=45 LSB in luma.

fixes.system: src/game/captureShots.js:410-419 bridge() camera + src/world/vegetation.js:495-497 blade LOD

fixes.system: src/render/canvasRenderPipeline.js — id-buffer edge test and the Attachment-1 outline resolve
fixes.problem: The outline pass has no anti-aliasing and it shows on every near-horizontal silhouette. Along the retaining-wall coping (x 1500..1560, y 458..486) the per-column darkest pixel alternates 57,61,62,68,78,91,97 and the per-column brightest alternates 120,201,127,180,159,155 — an 81 LSB swing between adjacent columns. Then attenuate ink with depth: `line *= mix(1.0, 0.20, smoothstep(0.05, 0.30, c.lz))` and lerp uInk toward uHazeColor by the same factor. Verification: along the coping the per-column max luma must vary by <20 LSB between adjacent columns, isolated-speckle count in (1300,560,600x140) must fall below 10, and the far-house patch meanEdge must drop below the near-stone 9.18.

fixes.system: src/world/worldMaterials.js:186-188 (npShadeCol) + the split-tone at src/render/canvasRenderPipeline.js:733-745
fixes.problem: Shade no longer carries albedo hue at all — it collapses to one violet regardless of material. Measured shade samples: dirt (110,90,119) hue 281, grass (134,112,139) hue 289, stone wall (123,104,133) hue 279, tank armour (70,53,76) hue 284 — a spread of 10 deg across four completely different albedos, while the same materials in light sit at hue 34, 54, 26 and 36 (spread 28 deg). `mix(npBase * uShadeTint, uShadeTint, 0.55)` throws away 55% of the albedo and `npShadeCol.b = max(npShadeCol.b, npShadeCol.r * 1.10)` then forces blue to lead on every surface. Frame-wide this makes the image a two-hue duotone: 69.3% of sampled pixels fall in hue 0-45, 26.0% in hue 255-345, and 0.1% in the entire 60-210 arc. There is not one sage-green or teal-grey pixel in a Gallian countryside shot; round 1 scored temperature 5 for warm-neutral shade and the fix has overshot into a global lavender grade.

In the grade, cut uShadowTint strength by half (raise the smoothstep to `smoothstep(0.0, 0.70, l)`) since it is the third violet multiply in the stack. Verification: shaded grass must land in hue 70-110 and shaded dirt in hue 20-45, and the frame hue histogram must place >=12% of pixels in 60-140 deg with <=12% in 255-345.

fixes.system: src/world/terrain.js:523 (`_col.lerp(shadeTint, (1 - ao) * 0.40)`) + src/world/worldMaterials.js:140-150 (bandify)
fixes.problem: The washes are not flat and the boundaries are not soft — both halves of axis 2 fail. (a) A continuous per-vertex AO ramp is baked into the terrain albedo BEFORE quantisation, so it survives it: inside one violet shade mass the luma ramps 122->82 (40 LSB) with zero plateaus, and the blobs visibly ripple internally at 2x zoom. On the flat-albedo retaining wall (1270-1560, 545-700) the blurred histogram is completely continuous — every 2-luma bucket from 58 to 210 is occupied at 1.0-1.5%, i.e. a single-material plane spans 152 LSB with no step anywhere. (b) uEdge 0.055 with no screen-space AA term gives a raw thresholded edge: single-pixel 53-LSB jumps (88,88,141,143 at y=1040) fringed with dither speckle.
fixes.change: Stop baking AO into albedo: quantise it first (`ao = floor(ao * 3.0 + 0.5) / 3.0` before the lerp) or move it out of the vertex colour and into npShade so the quantiser can eat it. In bandify, make the boundary width adaptive so it is always a ~1.2 px soft pigment edge rather than a hard threshold: `float aa = fwidth(sc) * 0.9; float w = max(uEdge, aa); return (f + smoothstep(0.5 - w, 0.5 + w, fr)) / uBands;`. Add a third warp octave at `npPx * 0.045` weighted 0.25 into npWarp so the boundary breaks into 6-15 px lobes instead of tracking the ground detail's horizontal streaks. Verification: a blurred vertical scan down the wall at x=1400 must show >=3 plateaus of >=12 samples within +/-2 LSB, and no transition may complete in under 2 px.

fixes.system: src/world/worldMaterials.js:201-218 (hatch block)
fixes.problem: The hatch is a pair of pure sine fields — `sin((npPx.x*0.819 + npPx.y*0.574) * 0.52 + npWob)` and its cross partner — so every stroke is a smooth sinusoidal ridge of identical amplitude that runs edge to edge across the whole wash with no start, no stop, no pressure change and no tooth. On the retaining wall and the tank hull it reads as a ruled mechanical screen laid over the fill (visible at 4x as unbroken diagonals crossing panel lines, tracks and stone courses alike), which is the rubric's printed-halftone failure rather than graphite.
fixes.change: Give each stroke a life: quantise the stroke index `float si = floor((npPx.x*0.819 + npPx.y*0.574) * 0.52 / 3.14159)`, hash it, and use the hash to (a) offset phase, (b) scale amplitude 0.55-1.0, and (c) cut the stroke into 20-70 px segments with `smoothstep` ends along the stroke direction so lines break. Replace `smoothstep(0.24, 0.72, npL1)` with a hard-cored profile (`smoothstep(0.45, 0.55, npL1) * (0.6 + 0.4 * grain)`) so a stroke has a dark core and a ragged edge instead of a sine ramp. Verification: run-length of continuous hatch along a stroke must average under 80 px, and stroke amplitude sd across strokes must exceed 25% of the mean.

command.tell: The entire ground plane is tiled with a hard-edged parallelogram lattice at a ~50 px pitch (FFT peak at fy=0.020 c/px; median-9 transects at y=890 step −9.2 lum at x=819, +8.7 at x=827, −6.8 at x=884 across perfectly straight diagonals) — that is Gouraud-interpolated per-vertex colour on decimated LOD triangles showing through as visible mesh faceting, an artefact no painting can produce and which no amount of paper grain on top disguises.

fixes.system: src/render/materials.js (lines 455, 524-532) + src/render/shaderLib.js vcQuantiseBands (line 241)
fixes.problem: ROUND 1'S HEADLINE DEFECT IS UNFIXED. The source shows a full rewrite (dPerPx at 463, wetBands at 524, vcQuantiseBands at 529, with comments explicitly citing 'Round 1'), yet the frame still measures as a continuous ramp with ZERO plateaus. Median-15 transect across the open grass at y=750, x=1200..1440: 189 188 187 189 191 191 185 176 170 170 170 173 175 176 174 173 172 171 171 170 166 164 165 165 169 180 188 192 194 195 — single-unit steps end to end. Sunlit road far, y=295, x=1500..1900: 184 174 175 171 169 167 162 162 170 174 175 178 177 174 ... 133 126 124 121 116 115 113 110 — a 74-lum ramp with no step exceeding 4. Across every smooth surface frac(|dL|>4) is 0.41%-3.28%. Ground-luminance histograms are single broad unimodal humps with no valleys (lower-left field: continuous 152→194, peak 8.4% at 176; right field 149→203). The cause is that `drive = keyN*uKeyGain + ambTerm*uFillGain + punctN` (line 455) is near-constant over near-planar terrain under a high sun, so the whole map lands inside one band, and ALL visible tonal variation then comes from per-vertex albedo and pigment texture applied AFTER quantisation — unquantised. The wet-edge machinery is real code doing nothing visible.
fixes.change: Quantise the composite luminance, not the light term. After `col` is assembled (post band-index colour grade, ~line 540), recover `float y = vcLum(col)`, quantise THAT with `vcQuantiseBands(y, 4.0, ...)` and rescale `col *= banded/max(y,1e-4)`, so albedo variation is forced onto the same 4 plateaus instead of riding over them. Additionally fold geometry into `drive` before the first quantise so flat ground still crosses boundaries: `drive = drive*(0.70 + 0.30*aAO) - 0.16*curvature`, curvature from the depth/normal derivative. Verify by re-running the y=750 transect: a pass shows ≥8 px runs at 4 distinct levels with <2 lum internal variation and jumps of 12-20 lum between them.

fixes.system: src/world/terrain.js — _buildTileGeometry(i0, j0, cells, step) (line 587) and the `color` BufferAttribute (line 671)
fixes.problem: AUTOMATIC REJECTION: visible faceting / obvious tiling period. The terrain colour is a per-vertex attribute Gouraud-interpolated across LOD-decimated cells. At the command camera (128 M across 1920 px, 0.44 m per base cell = 6.7 px) the visible facet pitch is ~50 px, i.e. step≈8 decimation, so the albedo field is sampled at 1/8 rate and every triangle pair reads as a flat parallelogram with a hard straight seam. It is unmistakable across the whole pale path and the grass at x 760-1160, y 780-1000 (crop attached region), with facet-to-facet deltas of 6-9 lum after a 9 px median. This alone is disqualifying regardless of the shading.
fixes.change: Stop shipping terrain albedo as vertex colour. Bake the colour field into a world-space triplanar splat sampled per-fragment (blend weights from slope + a low-freq domain-warped mask) so it is resolution-independent, and delete the `col` BufferAttribute at line 671. If vertex colour must stay, force `step = 1` for any tile inside the command frustum (the LOD selector is choosing by distance-to-camera and the top-down camera makes every tile 'far'), and pick the LOD by projected screen-space cell size with a hard floor of 4 px/cell.

fixes.system: src/render/canvasRenderPipeline.js — uPaperStrength (line 655), tGrain sampling (lines 572-573), uHazeMax/uHazeDensity (lines 368-372)
fixes.problem: Two coupled tonal failures. (a) The paper profile is INVERTED relative to the brief: high-frequency std by tone bucket is 12.24 at lum 100-140, 10.43 at 140-170, 7.55 at 170-195 (the midtone, where it should peak), then 9.04 at 195-215 and 12.48 at 215-245 (the highlights, where it should be gone). Grain is weakest exactly where cold-press tooth should be strongest. (b) The frame is tonally crushed into a milky wash: 61.8% of all world pixels fall in lum 140-210, world p5=98 / p50=167 / p95=203, std 35.3, and depth cues run backwards — the farthest strip (y 0-60, x 1500-1900) measures meanEdge 8.58 / p99 76.0 against a foreground (y 800-1000, x 400-900) of meanEdge 8.63 / p99 58.5, so the horizon is locally crisper than the near ground. Shade also fails the temperature axis: the 100-125 lum shadow population averages RGB 127,113,109 — hue 12°, sat 0.07, R-B +18 — a neutral warm grey, and only 2.1% of the frame is violet-biased (B > mean(R,G) + 8).
fixes.change: Reweight the fibre multiply by a midtone window: `paper *= uPaperStrength * (1.0 - pow(abs(vcLum(color)*2.0-1.0), 1.6))` so it dies at both ends and peaks at 0.5 luminance. Raise uHazeMax so the far field genuinely loses contrast (target far p99 edge ≤ 0.55 x foreground p99) and drop uHazeDensity so the near-mid stays clean, giving a monotone contrast falloff with distance. Push the darkest ramp target from lum 98 (p5) down to ~62 and set uViolet so the deepest shade lands near RGB 74,66,92 (hue ~262, sat 0.16, B-R +18) instead of the current neutral warm grey.

fixes.system: src/render/canvasRenderPipeline.js:492-497 (depthScale / fat / thin) + src/actors/rig.js:934,946 (outlineWidth 1.15 / 0.9) + src/core/config.js:18 (outlineWidth 1.35)
fixes.problem: The ink is a uniform hairline over the whole frame. Detecting every pixel darker than both neighbours 3 px away by >16 LSB gives 13,834 horizontal ink runs, width distribution 1 px 46.1%, 2 px 41.0%, 3 px 12.9%, and NOTHING at 4 px or wider anywhere in the image. fixes.change: Set depthScale = mix(4.2, 0.5, smoothstep(3.0, 55.0, distM)) and drop the `max(1.0, ...)` floor on thin to `uOutlineWidth * 0.30` with the hairline expressed as ink WEIGHT (multiply its contribution by 0.45) rather than radius. Add a +/-0.55 px per-stroke width jitter driven by vcHash(floor(sPx/9.0)) plus a second stroke offset 1.5 px along the edge normal at 0.35 opacity for the double-stroke. Verification: the run-width histogram must place >=15% of runs at >=4 px, and the hero silhouette undershoot must exceed the far-house undershoot.

fixes.system: src/world/worldMaterials.js:56 (PALETTE.stone 0xa39a8c) + the stone bin's makeCanvasMaterial opts at src/world/worldMaterials.js:428 + src/world/structures.js buildBridge
fixes.problem: The bridge is ~25% of frame and every pixel of it is landing in the SHADE bands. PALETTE.stone is 0xa39a8c — hue 37, a warm grey — yet on screen the sunlit parapet measures (152,135,151) hue 306 sat 0.08 and the spandrel measures (139,122,137) hue 306 sat 0.07: identical hue, mean L 136.3 vs 124.0, a 9% delta. That means vcShadowColour(albedo, uViolet 0x5d5080) at materials.js:535 is grading the entire structure, the drive never reaches band index 3, and there is no lit band, no terminator and no quantisation on a quarter of the image. The new ashlar coursing (a genuine round-1 fix) is therefore rendered as a flat lavender engraving, and it is the coldest, most off-palette mass in a frame whose every other surface sits in hue 20-60.
fixes.change: On the stone bin pass keyGain: 1.15, contrast: 2.2, lightBias: +0.10, bands: 4, violet: 0.9, cream: 1.35, and change PALETTE.stone 0xa39a8c -> 0xc4b79e so the lit courses can reach a warm cream. Add a per-face key boost from the world-space normal so the parapet cap (N.y > 0.7) gets drive * 1.25. Verification: the parapet cap must measure hue in [30,55] with sat >= 0.14 and L >= 175, the arch soffit must measure hue in [255,285], and a horizontal scan along the spandrel at y=520 must show >= 2 plateau boundaries with >= 25 LSB steps.

fixes.system: src/render/canvasRenderPipeline.js (final grade / bloom tint) + src/world/sky.js (PALETTE.skyZenith, skyHorizon)
fixes.problem: The palette has collapsed from round 1's over-saturation into monochrome sepia. Binning every chromatic pixel (chroma > 8) into 10 deg hue buckets puts 62.4% of the frame in hue 20-60 (30 deg alone = 24.8%); mean saturation is 0.210, median chroma 32. The sky is pure sepia top to bottom — (238,230,207) at y=40 through (248,217,168), (243,215,169), (235,211,169) at x=980, and (189,169,149)/(213,193,167)/(211,193,170) at x=250 — hue 25-35, sat 0.24-0.32, with no teal anywhere and no cloud form. The 'sage/olive' grass is hue 47-58 at sat 0.09-0.22, i.e. khaki, not green. VC Remastered separates cream highlights, sage-green foliage, ochre earth and a distinctly teal-grey sky; this frame has one hue family plus a lavender bridge.
fixes.change: Set PALETTE.skyZenith to 0x7d99a1 and PALETTE.skyHorizon to 0xe8d8b4 for >= 40 LSB zenith-to-horizon delta and >= 12% chroma at zenith, and quantise cloud shading to 3 steps through the same bandify() the world uses. Then split the two-tone grade: raise uCream 0xfff2d6 toward 0xfff0c8 for the lit bands but rotate the MID band's hue by -18 deg toward green for any material tagged foliage/terrain, so grass lit lands at hue 70-90 sat 0.22-0.30 instead of hue 47. Verification: no single 10 deg hue bucket may hold more than 14% of chromatic pixels, and the frame must contain >= 8% of chromatic pixels in hue 170-220.

fixes.system: src/actors/character.js (head/face feature emission, hand-to-weapon solve) + src/render/lighting.js (contact/ground anchoring)
fixes.problem: Form is still round 1's failure. The hero at 9 m has no face — the head is a blank tan oval under the helmet with no eye line, no brow and no jaw stroke. His right hand is an undifferentiated olive lozenge against the rifle with no wrist or cuff. The three 'Imperial Sturmtruppe' at 40-60 m are brown smudges with no readable silhouette at all. And round 1's headline for this shot is only half-addressed: the boot/ground seam still has no contact darkening — a vertical probe at x=1500 crossing the boot into the ground reads 71,73,72,66,70,72,68,71,72,76,65,68,70,73,71,69,75,74 with no local minimum at the seam, and the surrounding ground is uniformly the shade band, so the figure is anchored by nothing but occlusion.
fixes.change: Emit a screen-space feature pass from the head mesh into the outline weight channel: brow + upper-lash stroke and a 2 px iris dot with a 1.5 CSS px floor so the eye line survives to 45 m, plus a jaw crease at 0.5 weight. Drive the hand from the weapon's grip socket via two-bone IK rather than posing hand and rifle independently, and unhide the forearm/cuff geometry. Add a screen-space contact shadow in the fragment stage: 10-step ray march along L in view space, max length 0.30 m, thickness threshold 0.045 m, multiplied into the N.L term BEFORE banding at materials.js:455. Verification: the pixel row immediately under each boot must be >= 14 LSB darker than the same row 60 px lateral.

fixes.system: src/world/props.js / src/world/layout.js (telegraph wire geometry) + src/render/canvasRenderPipeline.js outline composite
fixes.problem: The telegraph wire across the upper right is sub-pixel geometry rendered as an on/off stipple, which is an automatic rejection ('aliased edges', 'lines must not crawl or shimmer'). Row y=209, x1755-1775 reads 180,94,103,118,203,210,189,193,207,194,102,83,92,123,181,168,85,93,102,172 — the wire is present for 2-3 px, absent for 4-6 px, and row y=210 has a completely different dot phase. In motion this will sparkle. The same class of artefact was flagged on the closeup in round 1 and has not been addressed.
fixes.change: Replace the wire line/thin-cylinder with a screen-facing ribbon: build it as a camera-billboarded quad strip whose half-width is max(worldRadius, 0.85 * mPerPx) evaluated per vertex, so it is never narrower than ~1.7 CSS px on screen, and fade its alpha by smoothstep(0.9, 1.8, screenPxWidth) so it dissolves into a wash instead of stippling when it does go sub-pixel. Exclude it from the id-buffer outline pass (userData.outline = false) and draw it as a single graphite stroke with the catenary sag baked into the geometry. Verification: the row scan at y=209 must show one contiguous dark run per wire with no gap wider than 1 px.
